title: OpenAI cuts the small-model API price
body: OpenAI lowered the API price of its small model by 20 percent on Tuesday. The new rate applies to developers using the public API. The company said the change is effective immediately.

title: NVIDIA launches a new accelerator
body: NVIDIA released the Blackwell Ultra accelerator for training clusters. The chip is available to server makers this quarter. NVIDIA said volume shipments begin in June.

title: Microsoft sets an annual infrastructure budget
body: Microsoft announced capital expenditure of 80 billion dollars for AI infrastructure in the current fiscal year. The figure covers data centers, chips, and networking equipment. The company disclosed the number on its earnings call.

title: Amazon agrees to buy a chip startup
body: Amazon agreed to acquire Northwind Silicon for 400 million dollars in cash. The deal is expected to close next quarter. Amazon said the team will join its cloud silicon group.

title: Anthropic closes a new round
body: Anthropic raised 2 billion dollars in a funding round led by existing investors. The company said the capital will pay for training runs. The round closed on Monday.

title: Meta starts a Louisiana data center
body: Meta announced a new data center campus in Richland Parish, Louisiana. The site will add 200 megawatts of capacity for model training. Construction starts in November.

title: Google releases a new Gemini model
body: Google released Gemini Flash to the public API today. Developers can call the model in every region where the Gemini API is already offered. Google published the model card alongside the launch.

title: DeepSeek posts a higher math score
body: DeepSeek reported that its latest model scored 89 percent on the MATH benchmark, up from 71 percent for the previous model. The company published the evaluation script. The comparison uses the same test set.

title: Mistral opens access to a new model
body: Mistral said Magistral is now generally available to every API customer. Accounts that already have a key can call it without joining a waitlist. The weights remain hosted by Mistral.

title: A smaller token bundle
body: OpenAI changed the way invoices are calculated for the mini model. A million input tokens that cost 1.50 dollars last month now cost 0.75 dollars under the new bundle. The company described the change as a packaging update for existing customers.

title: Amazon tells investors about next year's spend
body:
Amazon told investors it will spend 25 billion dollars on AI infrastructure next year. The sentence is the disclosure. The rest of this memo is office logistics and should not be read as a second announcement.

The program office booked conference room 4 for the weekly planning review. The notes from that review cover seating, lunch orders, and whose turn it is to take minutes. The minutes mention document titles and due dates for internal drafts. The calendar invite has no guest speakers. The facilities team will unlock the room at eight. This paragraph is about the meeting rather than a commercial announcement.

After the review, the group walked through a checklist for the shared drive. It covers folder names, who can edit, and which draft is the latest. The checklist does not describe a customer, a contract, or a construction site. It asks people to rename files that still say final. The work is clerical.

On Thursday the documentation desk will read two internal guides out loud and mark awkward sentences. The guides explain how to file an expense for a taxi and how to request a new chair. The session has a fifteen minute break. Nobody is scheduled to present a number from finance.

In the afternoon the office manager will count badges and order sandwiches. The count is for people who already work in the building. The sandwich order is ham, cheese, and a vegetarian tray. The manager will send the total to the kitchen by email. The email is not a disclosure.

During the following week the same group will repeat the review with a different room. The agenda is attendance, action items, and the date of the next review. The action items are all about documents and calendars. The date is a Tuesday. The note ends there.

The archive copy of these logistics notes will sit in the planning folder. It exists so a new coordinator can see how the meetings run. The folder has no press release and no customer name. The coordinator is asked to keep the folder tidy. That is the whole instruction.

title: A power contract outside Dallas
body: Microsoft signed a contract to buy 150 megawatts of electricity for a new computing hall outside Dallas. The hall is being built to train models, and the utility filing lists the site as an addition to the Microsoft campus already there. The power starts flowing in 2027.

title: AMD sends first silicon to partners
body: AMD has begun sampling the MI400 accelerator to a handful of server partners. The parts are early production silicon, and partners were told they can measure boards but cannot publish results yet. AMD did not quote a list price.

title: Cohere and a bank expand a partnership
body: Cohere and First Harbor Bank said they will work together on internal assistants. In the same announcement, Cohere confirmed it had closed 500 million dollars of new financing last week. The bank is not an investor in that financing. The assistants will be piloted in two departments.

title: Staff machine learning engineers
body: The lab is hiring staff machine learning engineers in London and Seattle. The roles focus on evaluation tooling and dataset review. Applications close at the end of the month. No product change was announced.

title: Research offsite in Lisbon
body: The research group will hold its annual offsite in Lisbon next March. The agenda is talk rehearsals and planning. Attendance is limited to full-time researchers. Travel is booked through the usual vendor.

title: How to tokenize a paragraph
body: This tutorial shows how to split a paragraph into tokens with a small Python function. It uses the standard library and prints the token count. The example text is about rivers and boats. Nothing in the walkthrough describes a company announcement.

title: Agenda for the autumn forum
body: The autumn forum opens at nine with registration. A panel on developer tools follows at half past ten. Lunch is at half past twelve. Office hours with the documentation team are at three. The schedule does not include product launches.

body:

title: Patch for a logging bug
body: Version 1.4.2 fixes a bug that wrote request identifiers into local debug logs. Users should upgrade at their next maintenance window. The patch does not change prices, models, or capacity. It is a maintenance update of the client library.

title: OpenAI ships a model and cuts its price
body: OpenAI released Harbor, a new small model, to all API customers this morning. In the same post, OpenAI lowered the price of Harbor input tokens by 30 percent versus the model it replaces. Both changes are live.

title: Microsoft pairs a budget with a new site
body: Microsoft announced 40 billion dollars of capital expenditure for AI infrastructure. The company also announced a new data center in Wisconsin to be built with that budget. The site is separate from existing campuses.

title: Adept raises money and buys a team
body: Adept raised 300 million dollars in a Series C. Separately, Adept acquired a ten-person compiler team from a studio called Larkline. The financing and the purchase were announced on the same day.

title: NVIDIA chip and a measured gain
body: NVIDIA released the H200 accelerator to cloud providers. NVIDIA also reported that models trained on the H200 scored 12 points higher on MMLU than the same models on the previous chip. The measurement used a fixed software stack.

title: A crowded product morning
body: Google, Amazon, Meta, Microsoft, Anthropic, and OpenAI each sent a speaker to the morning session, and none of them announced a product. CoreWeave then made three announcements of its own. CoreWeave released a model called Forge. CoreWeave cut the Forge API price by 15 percent. CoreWeave announced a new data center in Norway.

title: A price cut that did not happen
body: Traders circulated a note claiming that OpenAI had cut API prices overnight. OpenAI said the note is false and that prices are unchanged. No price change, model launch, or financing occurred. The company asked partners to disregard the rumor.

title: Only one vendor moved
body: Both OpenAI and Anthropic were mentioned in a market recap. Anthropic left its API prices unchanged. OpenAI lowered the price of its mini model by 10 percent. The recap says Anthropic has not followed.

title: Two figures for the same cut
body: The first paragraph says OpenAI reduced the mini-model price by 20 percent. A later correction in the same article says the reduction was 5 percent and that the 20 percent figure was a draft. The article still states that OpenAI did reduce the price. It does not name a second company.

title: A price cut that is only a scenario
body: If OpenAI were to cut API prices by half, startups would rewrite their budgets. The company has not done so. This note is a planning exercise for a customer, and no announcement has been made. Prices today are the same as last month.

title: Who changed the Azure price
body: The OpenAI model is sold through Microsoft on Azure. A blog post says the Azure price for that model fell by 18 percent. The post is signed by Microsoft and says OpenAI did not change the price on the OpenAI API. The company that changed the price is Microsoft.
